chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ali ibn Abu Abdullah, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying, and Abu Haneefah had said to him, 'The people were astonished at you yesterday while you were at Arafat, haggling over your sacrificial camels with the most intense bargaining.' He said, so Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'And what is the Pleasure of Allah if I am cheated in my wealth?' He said, so Abu Haneefah said, 'No, by Allah! There is little or much Pleasure of Allah in this, and we do not come to you with anything except that you come to us with what there is no way out for us from.'

key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: Arafat, the plain near Mecca where the standing (wuquf) of Hajj takes place
key_terms.لَا مَخْرَجَ لَنَا مِنْهُ: There is no way out for us from it

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq haggle over the price of sacrificial animals at Arafat?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the practical wisdom of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in economic transactions, illustrating his mastery of market dynamics during Hajj. Abu Haneefah’s admission that the Imam’s arguments were 'inescapable' underscores the depth of Shia jurisprudential reasoning in daily life. The narrative serves as a critique of rigid scholarly pride, emphasizing that maximizing one's wealth is not merely a worldly concern but aligns with divine pleasure when done justly.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ali Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Husayn Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying, and Abu Haneefa had said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The people were astonished from you<sup>asws</sup> yesterday in Arafaat haggling for your sacrificial animal with an intense bargaining’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘And what would be the Pleasure from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> if I<sup>asws</sup> were to incur a loss in my<sup>asws</sup> own wealth?’ 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So Abu Haneefa said, ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! There is no Pleasure from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in this, neither little nor more, and we do not come with anything except that he<sup>asws</sup> comes to us with what there is no way out for us from it’.
en.sarwar: 30. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah from al-Husayn ibn Yazid who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, in response to abu Hanifah who said to the Imam, ‘Your bargaining so stringently to buy a badanah yesterday in ‘Arafat had astonished people about you . 5

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘It is because Allah does not become happy if I suffer loss in my belongings . 5 Abu Hanifah then said, ‘It is true, by Allah, He is not happy with such a thing, be it a small or large amount. However, we never bring before you anything but that you come up with something which leaves no channel of escape for us . ‘“
